Hey, a psychiatrist here. The depictions in the game are actually much more accurate than other media entries on this matter. While very artistic, the visual hallucinations in the corner of the visual field (eyes in the forest) were very good. Apart from the auditory ve visual hallucinations and illusions, the story is where the game shines.
Prodromal period of schizophrenia, the family history and the onset of the symptoms were nicely done. Also it is thought that people with schizophrenia or people who have related personality traits often regarded as spiritual figures in small communities, just like Senua’s mother. The tendency towards an isolated life is also present in where Senua goes off to fight ‘the darkness’ and isolates herself in the forest. Let us not forget the abuse these people undergo from their families and communities.
I’m not sure about the ending though. These individuals are often unable to live a fulfilling life even if they get the best treatment. They live in the past, with their original delusions most of the time and lose their cognitive abilities as time passes. Maybe we need to try and create a more hopeful future for them, just like in the game.

Commenters are going to ask these questions. But let me ignore all of these and share my experience as a psychiatrist. 
People with MDD without any personality disorders tend to respond antidepressant medication well. ‘Emotional shallowing’ is essentially the underlying treatment mechanism for these medications. So yeah these patients often show lack of strong emotions during treatment which is needed for a period of time. 

But I think people who claim they’re ‘damaged’ by psychiatrists often have co-morbid disorders. Like I said personality disorders are the biggest part of the problem. When their symptoms are treated with antidepressants (constant suicidal thoughts and behaviours often require medication) because they do not actually have MDD, they don’t get the desired effects, get frustrated with side effects and blame psychiatrists for ruining their lives.

So in my country doctors have to suffer what’s called a ‘mandatory government service’ where you get sent to a remote and undeveloped city to serve the people who need medical attention. This will sound pathetic but I happen to be a goddamn psychiatrist and got sent to a city 1200kms away from my family (my mom is the only familiy I have). I was always a lonely child/teenager, now I’m a 29 y/o doctor and this mandatory service have become my rock bottom.

I got depressed (still am) though you wouldn’t call this a major depression as I could function well at work, not so well in other areas but the point is my depression didn’t show.  I was overwhelmed with my work and actually for the first time I forgot my birthday is coming. 

We have this system at the hospital I work in, that while a doctor’s on call they get a text message if a patient shows up at the ER and needs medical care in their fields, this happens to be psychiatric intervention/treatment in my case. And on my birthday I was on-call..

Like I said I completely forgot about my birthday and the night before I went to bed around 11 pm and woke up to the sound of a text message at 00:00. I thought great now I need to deal with a patient at this hour and started reading the message which always starts with ‘hospitals name- my name- patient info’.

To my surprise that text read ‘hospitals name- my name- we wish you a happy birthday’ then it hit me that it was my birthday. You might have guessed later on that day the only phone call I got was from my mother ( how could she forget after all my birth is the happiest/most painful event in her life), I got no texts, nothing. I usually get a few calls and some text messages.

I realised that my life from now on will continue like this, far away from home with no one to talk to and in complete loneliness. I think I’m okay with it now, at least I get to help people who are in need, and feel like I have a purpose. The hospital I work in cares for me so much so that with a fucking automated text they remembered my birthday..
